title: LeanBio capability map
description: Schema for the four versioned enumerations in pipeline/leanbio/capability-map/: personas.json, use-cases.json, grand-questions.json, tool-gap.json, plus the citation list they share. One schema, five document types, selected by the top-level `kind`. Every document carries `version` (the capability-map release, semver) and `as_of` (ISO date). Tool references carry a status: EXISTS means the name is a tool in sim-engine/contract.json or on the delphisci MCP server; PARTIAL means it exists but does not answer the whole question; MISSING means no such tool exists and the name is a PROPOSAL, defined in tool-gap.json. A validator (build.mjs) enforces that EXISTS/PARTIAL names resolve to real tools and that MISSING names do not.

status.description: EXISTS: the name is in sim-engine/contract.json or the delphisci MCP server and answers the need. PARTIAL: real tool, incomplete answer; `note` must say what it does not do. MISSING: no such tool; the name is a proposal and must appear in tool-gap.json.

surface.description: Where the tool is reachable. `script` means a node script in the repo with no tool wrapper (so an agent cannot call it).

note.description: For EXISTS, what it gives this persona. For PARTIAL, what it does NOT give. For MISSING, the one-line need.

gap_id.description: Required when status is MISSING: the tool-gap.json entry that defines it.

scope.description: What this document does NOT establish. Mandatory on every served document, like the tool envelope's scope.

today.description: What they actually do today, without this system.

tools.description: The tools this persona needs. NEVER empty: a persona with no tool list is a persona we have not thought about.

is_us.description: True when this persona is a role inside this project rather than an outside user.

honesty.description: The thing this persona would most easily be misled about.

question.description: The question as a user would ask it, in their words.

sequence.description: The tool sequence, in order. Every entry names a real tool (EXISTS/PARTIAL) or is explicitly MISSING with a gap_id. This is the field the test checks.

load_bearing.description: Required when status is MISSING. true: without this tool the route cannot be walked at all, so the use case is not answerable today. false: the route produces an answer without it and this tool would improve or quantify that answer. This is the atomic judgement from which `answerable_today` is derived, kept per step so it is inspectable.

answerable_today.description: yes: every step EXISTS. partly: at least one PARTIAL and no MISSING, or a MISSING step that only improves the answer. no: a MISSING step is load-bearing. Derived and checked by build.mjs.

missing.description: tool-gap ids this use case waits on.

result.description: What actually came back, from a file in this repo. Not a hypothetical.

evidence.description: Repo paths or identifiers a reader can open.

does_not_establish.description: The honest limit of the answer this sequence produces.

uncomfortable.description: Marks a use case that is awkward for us: it exposes a gap, or its honest answer is 'we do not know'.

the_line.description: The statement of what Lean can and cannot do, repeated once at the top of the document because every entry below depends on it.

disputed.description: True when the literature actively disagrees; `dispute` then says what about.

formalisable_core.description: (a) The part that is a question of whether a conclusion follows from stated premises. `has_core: false` with a reason is a legitimate answer and the test accepts it.

strength.description: How much of the question the core covers. `narrow` is the honest answer for most of them.

claim.description: The conditional, written so the premises are visible.

settles.description: What a Lean proof of it would settle.

lean.description: Fully qualified declaration in this repo, if it exists.

empirical_remainder.description: (b) What no proof can settle. `has_remainder: false` would be an extraordinary claim and needs a reason; no entry in this file makes it.

share.description: How much of the question is left to measurement after the core is proved.

measurement.description: The measurement that would settle it, where one is identifiable.

in_repo.description: (c) What already exists here towards it. An empty array is allowed and means: nothing, honestly.

strength.description: real: it addresses this question. adjacent: it addresses a neighbour and could be pointed here. shape-only: the proof pattern is reusable but says nothing about this question yet.

tools_needed.description: (d) What a user would need to work on this question here.

open_problem_ids.description: Ids in open-problems/problems.json, so the two enumerations join.

ranking.description: Written by build.mjs: how the rank was computed, so it is not a hand-asserted order.

name.description: The proposed tool name, in this repo's naming style.

kind.description: tool: an MCP/CLI/HTTP surface over data we can reach. lean-module: a Lean file that must be written and proposed before any tool can serve it. data: a measurement set we do not have. integration: wiring to a system outside this repo.

need.description: The question it answers, in a user's words.

signature.description: name(args) -> result, concretely enough to implement.

reads.description: The files, endpoints or registries it would read. This is what makes `buildable` checkable.

effort.description: small: a day on existing data. medium: a week. large: a month or a new subsystem. research: nobody knows how yet.

needs_data.description: Data we do not have, named.

needs_lean_build.description: True when it runs a Lean build, so it can be stdio-only and never on the hosted server.

nearest_existing.description: Real tool names that come closest today, so a reader can see what is already half-done.

risk.description: How this tool could mislead if built carelessly. A tool whose failure mode is not stated should not be built.

unblocks.description: Written by build.mjs from the other three documents; never hand-edited.

not_gaps.description: Things a reader will expect to find in the gap list that are absent ON PURPOSE. Leaving these out would make the gap list look like an oversight instead of a decision.

owner.description: The thread or person who owns the decision, where there is one.

citations.description: key -> record. Keys are referenced from grand-questions.json.

verified_via.description: How the record was confirmed to exist. `crossref-reprint` means only a later reprint's DOI could be fetched, not the original. UNVERIFIED means we could not fetch it and the reader should not trust the details; a fabricated citation is the worst failure this repo has.

is_book.description: A book or lecture, verified through a monograph or reprint DOI rather than as an indexed article. Check the details against a copy before quoting.

quotable.description: Text seen in the fetched record (title or abstract), so a reader can tell we opened it.

side.description: For a disputed question, which side of the dispute this is.
